title: Etaleness of a supplied finite depth-two extension on a smooth local scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring with closed point $a$ and depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $U\subset L$ be open, contain every point not lying over $a$, and have dense inverse image in the scheme-theoretic closed fibre $L_a$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $p:E\to L$ be a supplied finite morphism, etale upon restriction over $U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume depth $\mathcal O_{E,z}\geq2$ whenever $p(z)\notin U$. Then $p$ is etale everywhere. The statement asserts no existence of E and no construction of an extension.

proof.text: Smoothness makes L locally Noetherian. Apply the formal-completion flatness theorem to the supplied finite extension p with haway, hclosed, hdepth and hboundary, obtaining Flat p.
Apply the flat finite depth-two formal-unramifiedness criterion to p and U. This uses only the source boundary depth; it does not require the smooth family or any target boundary depth calculation.

Finiteness over a locally Noetherian target gives local finite presentation by Mathlib instance synthesis. Combine Flat p, FormallyUnramified p and local finite presentation using Etale.of_formallyUnramified_of_flat.

theorem etale_of_smooth_local_depth_two_finite_extension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {L : Scheme.{u}} (q : L ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [Smooth q]
    (U : L.Opens)
    (haway : ∀ y : L, q y ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A → y ∈ U)
    (hclosed : Dense (↑((q.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)) ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
      Set (q.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A))))
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := A) A)
    {E : Scheme.{u}} (p : E ⟶ L) [IsFinite p] [Etale (p ∣_ U)]
    (hboundary : ∀ z : E, p z ∉ U →
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := E.presheaf.stalk z) (E.presheaf.stalk z)) :
    Etale p
